fields.fix: Use min-height for a floor, or let the content size the box.

fields.source: Modern CSS intrinsic layout — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the layout solve content and component sizing with fixed dimensions or breakpoint patches where intrinsic sizing could express the relationship?
fields.fix: Prefer min/max-content, fit-content, auto, flex/grid, clamp(), and content-sized controls before adding fixed dimensions or breakpoint overrides.

fields.source: CSS Container Queries — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does a reusable component respond to the viewport even though its actual constraint is the size of its containing component?
fields.fix: Use a named or nearest container query when the component's behavior depends on container size.

fields.ask: Does a form control use brittle fixed sizing where its content, label, validation state, or user input should determine its size?
fields.fix: Prefer intrinsic form sizing and field-sizing when it improves the control without harming predictability.

fields.source: Popover and dialog — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the interface recreate a disclosure, popover, or dialog primitive with unnecessary custom state and positioning?
fields.fix: Prefer semantic dialog, popover, details, and native open-state behavior when their contracts match the interaction.

fields.source: CSS Anchor Positioning — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Is a floating element positioned relative to another element through brittle coordinates or JavaScript when their spatial relationship is stable?
fields.fix: Prefer declarative anchor positioning where browser support and the interaction contract permit it.

fields.ask: Can a component's styles leak across unrelated DOM regions because its selectors are broader than its ownership boundary?
fields.fix: Prefer component-local selectors or @scope where it removes selector leakage without adding unnecessary abstraction.

fields.ask: Does a mobile layout assume a stable viewport height when browser chrome, safe areas, or the virtual keyboard can change the available space?
fields.fix: Use svh, dvh, lvh, env(safe-area-inset-*), and intrinsic layout according to the actual interaction requirement.

fields.source: CSS overflow and modern scroll containers — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the layout create accidental page overflow, nested scroll traps, or a scroll container that breaks sticky or touch interaction?
fields.fix: Give each scroll container one intentional axis and verify the rendered scroll and sticky behavior at mobile widths.

fields.source: Web accessibility and reduced motion — web.dev
fields.ask: Does motion ignore the user's reduced-motion preference or animate a state whose continuity can be communicated without motion?
fields.fix: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and keep transitions short, purposeful, and nonessential.

fields.source: View Transitions and Navigation API — Baseline 2026
fields.ask: Does a same-origin navigation or state transition unnecessarily destroy context when continuity would make the relationship between states clearer?
fields.fix: Preserve scroll, focus, state, and visual continuity first; use View Transitions or the Navigation API only when they simplify a real transition.

fields.source: Web rendering performance — compositor-safe interaction motion
fields.ask: Does frequent interaction motion stay on transform and opacity where possible, avoid layout properties such as top/width/height, and avoid permanent will-change or expensive visual effects?
fields.fix: Animate transform and opacity for interaction feedback; let layout properties remain stable, and add will-change only around a measured animation boundary when it removes a real hitch.
fields.good: .card { transition: transform var(--duration-m3-short) var(--ease-m3-spring), opacity var(--transition-fast) var(--ease-out); }

fields.source: Interaction feedback — loading, success and failure are observable states
fields.ask: Does an action expose a coherent state sequence such as idle → working → success/failure, with the final state remaining understandable after motion stops? Do not rely on color, motion, or a short-lived flash as the only evidence.
fields.fix: Give each important action an explicit state, choreograph its transition with the shared motion tokens, and keep a static success or failure representation for reduced motion.
fields.bad: Tap Pay; briefly spin; disappear with no persistent result.
fields.good: Tap Pay → working state → self-drawing success mark or persistent failure state; all meanings remain available without motion.

fields.source: Pointer Events and touch-action — gesture ownership
fields.ask: Does a drag or swipe surface explicitly declare which pan remains with the browser and which axis belongs to the interaction? A direct-manipulation gesture must not compete silently with page scrolling, navigation gestures, or pull-to-refresh.
fields.fix: Declare touch-action on the gesture surface: use pan-y for horizontal swipes in a vertical page, pan-x for vertical rails, or none when the interaction deliberately owns both axes. Keep an equivalent keyboard/control path.

fields.source: DENSITY — a small tracked all-caps line above a heading restates the heading's role; Strunk, omit needless words
fields.fix: Drop the eyebrow; let the heading and the page structure say where the reader is. A label that names a field stays.

fields.source: DENSITY — a link already says it can be followed; an arrow glyph in its text adds no information
fields.fix: Write the verb and the object ("Les saken"); the link styling carries the affordance.

fields.source: LINEARITY — structure belongs to the element tree; glyphs between words make a flat string the reader must parse
fields.fix: Put each fact in its own element (a list item or a span) and let spacing or a border separate them.

fields.source: RENDERED_VALUES and flat design — a gradient wash is a colour the operator did not choose; surfaces are flat tokens
fields.fix: Paint the surface with its token colour. A fade to transparent over an edge or a scrim under text is allowed.

fields.source: LINEARITY — a 01, 02, 03 marker promises a sequence; on items with no order it is decoration
fields.fix: Drop the number, or make the items an ordered list when the order is real.

fields.source: pub4 visual identity contract — signal colour is a semantic marker, never a general surface or body-text colour
fields.fix: Use the signal only as a selected-state marker with explicit signal ink; use the local product accent for ordinary buttons, page surfaces and text.

fields.source: MASTER post-incident /fix hardening — finite convergence ranks
fields.fix: Use a finite sentinel or score_value before integer coercion; never call to_i/to_int on a non-finite float.

fields.source: MASTER post-incident /fix hardening — extract-then-match regex integrity
fields.fix: Match the extracted regex body with regex syntax appropriate to the body; do not add source-level escaping twice.
Add role= and tabindex= for accessibility.

fields.source: style.yml bare_tag_targeting — the tag is already the name
fields.fix: Drop the filler class and select the bare tag; a prefix that names which of several coexisting elements this is may stay.

fields.fix: Replace literal with t('.key').

fields.source: HTML Living Standard — meta charset utf-8 (WHATWG)
fields.fix: Add a UTF-8 charset declaration as the first element in head.

fields.source: CSP script-src / separation of concerns — assets are files
fields.fix: Move it to an asset file and reference it with javascript_include_tag or stylesheet_link_tag.

fields.source: CSP / separation of concerns — no inline styles
fields.fix: Extract to CSS class; pass dynamic values as custom properties.
Replace the selector call with a Stimulus target or querySelector.

fields.source: CSS naming — classes name meaning, not appearance
fields.fix: Name the role, not the rendering — or use the element that already means it (small, strong, em, time).
Use <header>, <footer>, <nav>, <main>, <aside>, <article>, <section>.
Add a skip link to #main-content in the layout.
Move layout to SCSS with bare tag targeting.

fields.ask:
Do every MASTER-to-model council turn use InterModelContract to construct a structured request envelope,
attach a SHA-256 artifact reference, validate the returned JSON finding schema, and record a bounded metric
without persisting raw model text? Invalid output must receive one structured rejection and one retry only.
fields.practice: Treat other models as protocol peers: explicit authority, evidence, bounded artifacts, structured disagreement, and no reciprocal persona.
fields.fix: Wrap every council model request with InterModelContract and validate its returned structured findings before aggregation.
Use async/await for readability.

fields.source: Airbnb JS Style Guide — for...of over for...in
fields.fix: for...in iterates prototype properties. Use for...of.

fields.source: Airbnb JS Style Guide — no var (ES6 let/const)
fields.fix: Use const (default) or let (when reassigned).
Use ?? when 0 or '' are valid values.
Rewrite to obj?.foo?.bar

fields.source: Airbnb JS Style Guide — template literals (ES6)
fields.fix: Use `Hello ${name}!` template literals.
One point, one pixel: gl_PointSize=1.0. Put depth and curvature into brightness, not size.

fields.source: pixel_perfection forbidden_css: soft glow — the WebGL spelling of it
fields.fix: Delete the additive pass. Brightness states form; a second offset pass is a glow.
fields.bad: transparent: true, depthWrite: false, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending

fields.source: Haptic interaction feedback — optional secondary signal
fields.ask: When haptic feedback is used, is it attached to a meaningful user action or threshold, fired at the start of direct manipulation when appropriate, gracefully unavailable, power-conscious, and never the only confirmation?
fields.fix: Keep haptics short and optional, trigger them only for meaningful interactions, suppress them when the page is hidden or the device is power-constrained, and preserve a visible or semantic equivalent.
fields.bad: navigator.vibrate([100,100,100,100,100]) for every hover or pointermove
fields.good: pointerdown → brief tick; commit → success pattern; unsupported or suppressed → visible feedback remains

fields.ask: Does a direct-manipulation interaction acknowledge pointer input at pointerdown or an equivalent active state instead of making a click handler carry all perceived responsiveness? Preserve keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.
fields.fix: Move only the immediate acknowledgement to pointerdown/active state; leave the actual command and confirmation semantics on the existing action path.

fields.source: Shared RAILS haptics controller — one tactile implementation
fields.ask: Does Rails interaction code use the shared haptics implementation instead of reaching directly for navigator.vibrate, so suppression, timing and future native adapters remain one source of truth?
fields.fix: Import the shared pub4/haptics controller or its pulse API. Keep raw navigator.vibrate behind that shared implementation.

fields.practice:
before adding machinery, run the universal transformation plan in
data/laws.yml#transformation_policy. inventory and classify first, then
follow its declared order and operation descriptions without maintaining
a second sequence here. recommend rather than mutate when proof is
insufficient. adding is the last resort and its reason belongs in git
history. Every kept transformation refreshes the corpus before repair
resumes.
fields.fix: before writing a new file, class, or dependency, try nine moves first and in this order.

fields.ask: Does this unit introduce unnecessary complexity?
fields.practice:
fewest moving parts that solve the problem. when a simpler shape does the
job, propose it instead of building the one you were asked for, and delete
abstractions until it hurts.
fields.fix: Delete abstractions until it hurts. KISS.
fields.bad: a factory, a registry and an adapter for one call site

fields.ask: Does this code edit proceed before the complete target source and relevant dependencies, callers, loaders, configuration, tests and public contracts have been read and understood?
fields.practice:
never rewrite working code from a snippet. read the complete current target
and its dependency/caller/test/configuration contract before writing, using
content hashes and a fresh reference map as evidence. A cached excerpt,
assumed caller list or graph that failed to read a source is not complete
understanding. If relevant context is missing or exceeds the safe context
budget, stop that repair as BLOCKED or HUMAN_DECISION rather than guessing.
preserve behavior and intent, and take a larger change only when it is
justified and tested.
fields.fix: Read the entire target and its relevant dependencies before editing; preserve behavior and prove the change.
fields.bad: edits a forty-line excerpt without reading the complete source or its callers
fields.good: reads the whole source, traces dependency and caller files, then changes only the justified lines

fields.ask: Does this unit contain unnecessary verbosity in words, tokens, structure, or output?
fields.practice:
omit needless words and omit needless code. if the answer is one word, say
one word.
fields.fix: Omit needless words. Omit needless code.

fields.practice:
hold register, density, and length consistent across a session; shift only
when the user shifts.
fields.fix: hold register, density, and length consistent across a session;
fields.good: the same register the session opened in

fields.practice:
match vocabulary to the user's demonstrated tier; gloss every new term on
first use.
fields.fix: match vocabulary to the user's demonstrated tier;
fields.good: the term, then what it means, once

fields.practice: failures and blockers lead the response; context and explanation follow.
fields.fix: failures and blockers lead the response;
fields.bad: context first, failure in the last line

fields.practice: every closed door names an adjacent open one.
fields.fix: every closed door names an adjacent open one.
fields.good: cannot do that; here is the adjacent thing I can

fields.practice:
answer the one obvious follow-up question in the same response; no second
round-trip.
fields.fix: answer the one obvious follow-up question in the same response;

fields.practice:
read the man page or upstream reference docs before using any command,
config file, framework, operating system, or programming language.
Training-data assumptions about flags, syntax, and behavior are unreliable
— verify against the source.
fields.fix: read the man page or upstream reference docs before using any command, config file, framework, operating syste

fields.practice:
a clean result is a claim about the measurement, not about the code.
Before acting on "no callers", "no findings", "0 unread", re-run without
the filter that produced it and confirm the check can still see a
known-positive case. Every self-inflicted break on 2026-08-10 came from a
check that was measuring nothing and said so as a pass — a grep whose
`grep -v` hid the three callers it was clearing, a source scan that
matched the comment explaining a rule rather than the rule, and two
baselines still granting exemptions to a deleted file.
fields.fix: a clean result is a claim about the measurement, not about the code.
fields.good: re-runs without the filter that produced it

fields.practice:
a recorded finding states where and what, and is routinely wrong about
both. Re-measure before fixing. Of 129 hardcoded_copy findings, 38 were
already translated one branch away, 8 named the first of two occurrences
in their file, and 1 was hardcoded Norwegian a literal-matching rule
cannot tell from English. Fixing a stale finding list edits code that was
already right.
fields.fix: a recorded finding states where and what, and is routinely wrong about both.
fields.bad: fixes every line the list names
fields.good: re-measures, then fixes what is still there

fields.practice:
an allowlist entry, baseline row or opt-out that outlives its subject is a
hole in a check nobody can see, because the thing it excuses is invisible.
Every exemption names what it excuses, and a check fails when the named
thing stops existing.
fields.fix: an allowlist entry, baseline row or opt-out that outlives its subject is a hole in a check nobody can see, beca
fields.bad: an allowlist entry outliving its subject
fields.good: an exemption naming what it excuses, checked

fields.practice:
when a scan finds violations, sweep to convergence rather than pausing for
per-fix confirmation. One approved direction runs the whole backlog. "Ship
all", "yes", "do it", "kill X keep Y" are binding. Ask before destructive
shared-state edits, material ambiguity, or a genuine either-or.
fields.fix: when a scan finds violations, sweep to convergence rather than pausing for per-fix confirmation.
fields.good: runs the backlog and reports once

fields.practice:
run the probes, checks, tests and fixes here. Never close with "you should
run X" when X is executable. Check stdout beats narrative completion; on
failure, diagnose and retry rather than handing the chore back. Commit and
push each owned, verified repair batch before moving on unless the operator
explicitly withholds publication or a safety/delivery guard blocks it.
fields.fix: Run the required proof, then commit and push each owned verified batch; report any blocked delivery.
fields.bad: leaves an accumulating uncommitted repair backlog and says to push it later
fields.good: commits and verifies a coherent repair checkpoint, pushes it, then continues

fields.practice:
"through" means deep scan the path and attempt every actionable finding,
then rescan and repeat until DONE or an explicit truthful terminal state.
No fixer, time limit, quota pause or failed pass proves everything was
repaired. Name every unresolved finding, exclusion, unmeasured surface and
human decision. Lint written paths and audit lib/ for drift after mutations.
fields.fix: Sweep every actionable finding and prove convergence; report every blocker and unresolved item.
fields.bad: one scan, then stops or reports success with unresolved findings
fields.good: repairs and rechecks every actionable finding, or names the precise non-DONE terminal state

fields.source: MASTER constitution — one source of truth and executable documentation
fields.ask: After a code change, are affected user documentation, interface contracts, configuration instructions and operations guidance reconciled, and have generated documents been regenerated from their canonical source?
fields.practice:
after every code change, reconcile the affected documentation in the same
repair batch. When behavior, public interfaces, commands, configuration or
operations change, update the relevant README/contract/runbook and regenerate
every affected generated document through its canonical generator. Never
hand-edit generated copies, and do not churn unrelated documents.
fields.fix: Update affected documentation and regenerate generated copies from the canonical source before closing the batch.
fields.bad: changes a command or interface but leaves its documented contract stale
fields.good: updates the affected README/contract and runs the canonical docs generator

fields.practice:
council is Review-stage deliberation with a Security veto. Run it on
dangerous patterns, multi-file diffs, or when config enables it. Scan plus
sweep is the default loop; council is conditional.
fields.fix: council is Review-stage deliberation with a Security veto.

fields.practice:
after an OPENBSD/ or RAILS/master/ edit, run bin/probe integrity before
declaring done. A failing check means the task is still open.
fields.fix: after an OPENBSD/ or RAILS/master/ edit, run bin/probe integrity before declaring done.

fields.practice:
one SSH session, no parallel bin/ci. Production truth is vm23. Copy any
edit made on the box back into git in the same session.
fields.fix: one SSH session, no parallel bin/ci.

fields.practice:
one file, one restart. After a RAILS/master, live lib/ or data YAML deploy,
restart and wait before curling. Never batch web edits behind a single
restart at the end.
fields.fix: one file, one restart.

heavy work belongs on the VPS. The Mac edits and HTTP-probes; browser
checks run on the deploy host unless explicitly forced local.
fields.fix: heavy work belongs on the VPS.
fields.good: browser checks on the deploy host

runtime-read material lives in data files, not prose. Top-level READMEs
are one-paragraph stubs pointing at runtime truth. When behaviour changes,
refresh the stub in the same commit.
fields.fix: runtime-read material lives in data files, not prose.

before copying a block to vary one literal, extract or parameterise it.
File and module sprawl is the same law one level up.

fields.practice:
edit the original path. No _fixed.rb, no staging copy, no new file without
approval — try merge or rename first on every touch. Tree-level /fix checks
the name and ownership surface before it creates a new path.
fields.fix: edit the original path.

fields.practice:
no sed, awk, head, tail, find, wc, perl or python in agent shell

available. Prefer Baseline Widely available semantics for core paths; progressively enhance newer APIs such as
field-sizing, container style queries, contrast-color(), CSS anchor positioning, Trusted Types, and the
Navigation API. Verify the target browser matrix, feature detection, keyboard and assistive-technology
behavior, and a usable fallback. Do not make network access or a new package a build/test prerequisite.

fields.ask:

treat a Baseline Newly available feature as universal without a fallback?
fields.practice: Prefer accessible browser primitives and interoperable CSS over bespoke JavaScript and avoidable dependencies.
fields.fix:
Prefer semantic HTML, native form controls and browser APIs, CSS Grid/Flexbox, intrinsic sizing, and logical properties before
custom JavaScript or a new dependency. Default core paths to Baseline Widely available features. Use @supports or runtime feature
detection for newer capabilities, preserving a usable accessible fallback. At feature start, check current Baseline data and,
when available, consult GoogleChrome Modern Web Guidance for a focused implementation pattern. Do not make network access or
a guidance CLI a build/test prerequisite.

fields.ask: Does a mobile-first web change fail to reflow at 320 CSS pixels, hide keyboard focus, rely on pointer-only interaction, or ignore reduced motion?
fields.practice: Mobile-first means content and interaction survive narrow viewports, zoom, keyboard navigation, assistive technology, and touch.
fields.fix:
Require reflow without loss at 320 CSS pixels except for genuinely two-dimensional content. Meet WCAG 2.2's 24 by 24 CSS pixel
pointer-target criterion and its exceptions; prefer 44 CSS px for primary touch controls where the layout allows. Keep focus visible
and unobscured, labels and accessible names present, keyboard paths complete, and nonessential motion responsive to
prefers-reduced-motion. Use logical properties and intrinsic layouts; use safe-area insets and dynamic viewport units with sensible fallbacks.

fields.good: max-inline-size: 100%; min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; :focus-visible has an outline; reduced motion has a fallback.

fields.source: MDN Progressive Web Apps and service-worker caching guidance
fields.ask: Does a PWA assume optional APIs exist, offer no honest offline state, or cache or replay data without explicit freshness and safety rules?
fields.practice: An installable PWA is still a web application: navigation, online failure, user data, and updates need explicit semantics.
fields.fix:
Feature-detect optional install, sharing, storage, background, and navigation APIs and leave the primary task usable without them.
Keep deep links and a useful offline fallback. Prefer cache-first for versioned immutable assets and network-first with a bounded timeout
for mutable navigation/data; cache GET requests only under an explicit scope and freshness policy, never blindly cache personalized responses
in a shared cache. Queue writes only when necessary, with visible pending state, bounded storage, same-origin validation, and idempotent replay.
Treat a manifest, service worker, and install prompt as separate capabilities; test each supported path.
fields.bad: Cache every request and assume Background Sync, install prompts, and file sharing exist on all devices.
fields.good: Detect optional capabilities, cache by request type and freshness, offer an offline route, and retry only safe queued writes.

fields.ask: Does this file have dense blocks with no visual breaks, or ragged indentation?
fields.fix: One blank line between sections, never more than two consecutive.

fields.source: Release It! — retry budgets / bounded retries (Nygard)
fields.fix: Add max_attempts cap and exponential backoff.
fields.good:
next if action == :retry
def retry?(error, attempt:)
@bus&.publish("llm:failover_backoff", retry: retry_index + 1)
[+0.18, :name, /retry|loop|escalat/],
# a retry then spawned a duplicate on the same output file
attempts += 1 and redo if attempts < 3
message: "retry with no visible attempt counter",
lines << "refresh %s retry" % policy.dig("soa", "retry")

fields.source: MASTER-native — git holds history; comments hold reasons
fields.fix: State the present reason. Put the history in the commit message.
fields.good: # Bar names what it returns, so a caller can tell it from Baz.

fields.source: Clean Code / Code Complete — comments explain why, not what
fields.fix: Comments should explain intent, not restate the code.
fields.good: # retries are capped so a flapping host cannot pin the worker

fields.ask: Are IO, database, network, filesystem, or process side effects scattered deep inside business logic instead of isolated at the edges?
fields.fix: Return values from the core and move IO to the shell.

fields.ask: Does this require explicit configuration where an established local convention already provides the correct behavior?
fields.fix: Use the existing convention; add configuration only when it changes a real requirement.

fields.source: Optimize for Programmer Happiness (Rails Doctrine, DHH)
fields.ask: Does this design impose ceremony or friction that does not buy meaningful safety or clarity?
fields.fix: Remove unnecessary ceremony and keep the common path expressive.

fields.source: The Menu Is Omakase (Rails Doctrine, DHH)
fields.ask: Does this introduce a competing tool when the application already has a suitable integrated default?
fields.fix: Use the existing integrated default unless a concrete requirement justifies deviation.

fields.ask: Does this force one programming paradigm where a pragmatic combination would make the design clearer?
fields.fix: Mix paradigms where each fits the problem; do not enforce uniformity for ideology's sake.
fields.bad: class Pipeline; def call; steps.inject { |state, step| step.call(state) }; end; end

fields.ask: Would a reader find this merely correct rather than clear, coherent, and aesthetically deliberate?
fields.fix: Rewrite for structural and aesthetic clarity, not merely passing tests.
fields.bad: if a; b; else; c; end

fields.ask: Does this restrict a capable operator's legitimate power mainly to guard against a rare misuse?
fields.fix: Preserve useful capability; document dangerous edges and require deliberate use.

fields.ask: Does this fragment a cohesive concern into separate services or gems without a concrete boundary that justifies it?
fields.fix: Keep the concern integrated until an actual boundary, ownership, or scaling need requires extraction.

fields.ask: Is a beneficial breaking change being avoided solely to preserve compatibility when a clear upgrade path exists?
fields.fix: Take the justified breaking change and provide an explicit migration path.

fields.source: Push Up a Big Tent (Rails Doctrine, DHH)
fields.ask: Does this unnecessarily exclude contributors through needless cleverness, jargon, or unexplained conventions?
fields.fix: Prefer clear language and approachable structure without lowering technical rigor.
fields.bad: raise Foo::Bar::Baz unless x && y && z
fields.good: raise InvalidState, "x requires y and z" unless x && y && z

fields.ask: Is this splitting a cohesive application into services before a concrete extraction boundary or operational need exists?
fields.fix: Keep the feature in the application until extraction is clearly justified.

fields.ask: Does this module mix Result objects, exceptions, and nil returns for equivalent failure paths?
fields.fix: Choose one error strategy per module and use it consistently.
fields.bad: def find(id); raise NotFound if missing; end
fields.good: def find(id); Result.ok(record) or Result.err(:not_found); end

fields.ask: Does an answer depend on current, niche, uncertain, repository, browser, device, or externally verifiable facts without first selecting the evidence surface that can actually observe them?
fields.fix: Route the turn by evidence need: read/search the repository for repository facts, use device capability for local hardware, use browser capability for page state, and use local knowledge or current web sources for unfamiliar or time-sensitive facts; never substitute memory for available evidence.

fields.ask: Does verification rely only on regex or only on an LLM when the subject can be checked with both deterministic and semantic evidence?
fields.fix: Layer deterministic detection with semantic review where both add independent evidence.

fields.ask: Is a high-stakes creative or design decision accepting the first plausible draft without exploring alternatives?
fields.fix: Generate several materially different candidates, then curate against explicit constraints.

fields.ask: Does one conceptual change require edits across many unrelated files because the missing abstraction has no single home?
fields.fix: Create the missing abstraction or single source so one conceptual change has one owner.

fields.source: Clean Code — avoid global mutable state (R.C. Martin)
fields.ask: Are global variables or mutable class-level values shared across modules without explicit ownership?
fields.fix: Inject configuration and state through explicit boundaries.

fields.ask: Is infrastructure being built without first proving the simplest end-to-end path through the real system?
fields.fix: Wire the smallest end-to-end path first, prove it works, then add depth.
fields.bad: class Queue; end; class Worker; end; class Adapter; end

fields.ask: Does changing one dimension force unrelated changes in another, such as database details leaking into UI or style changing structure?
fields.fix: Decouple dimensions so changes remain local.

fields.ask: Is the design modeling work as scattered mutable state when it can be expressed as a clear sequence of transformations?
fields.practice: On a structural or prose cleanup, inventory and classify first; defragment, decouple, flatten, merge, split, relocate, rename, reorder, remove, reflow and simplify in that order, then prove preservation.
fields.fix: Express the flow as input-to-output transformations with explicit stages.

fields.source: A Philosophy of Software Design (John Ousterhout)
fields.ask: Is this module shallow, exposing a complex interface while doing little work behind it?
fields.fix: Absorb complexity behind a small interface that provides substantial capability.
fields.bad: service.call(a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h)

fields.ask: Is the same logic or data defined in multiple authoritative places?
fields.fix: Extract one authoritative representation and make all consumers reference it.

fields.ask: Are there implicit couplings between modules that should be explicit dependencies?
fields.fix: Inject dependencies through explicit boundaries; avoid hidden global state.

fields.ask: Does a partial dependency failure crash the whole operation when a bounded fallback is possible?
fields.fix: Use timeouts, circuit breakers, bounded retries, or a safe fallback.

fields.ask: Is a complex system being built from scratch without first proving a smaller working system?
fields.fix: Start with the simplest working system, prove it, then extend.
fields.bad: class Platform; def initialize; @services = 27.times.map { Service.new }; end; end
fields.good: class Platform; def call(input); MinimalPath.call(input); end; end

fields.ask: Is existing code being removed or changed without first understanding why it exists?
fields.fix: Read history, tests, callers, and rationale before removing it.

fields.source: Unix philosophy — do one thing well (Doug McIlroy)
fields.ask: Does one module perform several unrelated jobs that could compose through a clear boundary?
fields.fix: Split unrelated responsibilities into focused components and compose them.
fields.bad: class Report; def query; end; def render; end; def email; end; end

fields.ask: Are two units expressing the same knowledge independently rather than sharing one authoritative source?
fields.fix: Merge the duplicated knowledge or make one representation authoritative.

fields.ask: Does this introduce complexity the problem does not require?
fields.fix: Flatten the design to the simplest structure that solves the actual problem.

fields.ask: Do names, APIs, or behavior contradict what a reasonable reader would expect?
fields.fix: Rename or reshape the interface so behavior matches its apparent meaning.
fields.bad: users.empty? # returns true when users exist

fields.source: Refactoring code smell: Large Class / God Object (Fowler)
fields.ask: Does one class accumulate unrelated responsibilities that should have separate owners?
fields.fix: Decompose into focused objects with explicit responsibilities.
fields.bad: class Application; def users; end; def billing; end; def render; end; def mail; end; end
fields.good: class Users; end; class Billing; end

fields.source: MASTER-native — collapse before adding; flat hierarchy
fields.ask: Are tiny files or one-file directories adding structure without carrying meaningful independent responsibility?
fields.fix: Absorb tiny artifacts into their natural owner before creating another boundary.

fields.ask: Do implementation details leak across a module boundary so changing one decision forces unrelated callers to change?
fields.fix: Encapsulate the decision behind a stable interface.

fields.source: A Philosophy of Software Design — different layers, different abstractions
fields.ask: Do adjacent layers merely relay the same abstraction without transforming it?
fields.fix: Make each layer add a meaningful abstraction or remove the layer.

fields.ask: Does the artifact's structure contradict the conceptual shape of the problem?
fields.fix: Align modules, sections, layout, and boundaries with the actual domain.

fields.source: Boundaries (Gary Bernhardt) — values at the edges
fields.ask: Does a boundary assume perfect fidelity or that the other side will never change?
fields.fix: Translate and validate at boundaries; define safe degradation.

fields.source: A Philosophy of Software Design — complexity belongs behind the interface
fields.ask: Is complexity being pushed onto callers instead of absorbed by the implementation?
fields.fix: Move complexity behind a small, stable interface.

fields.source: The Pragmatic Programmer — Easier To Change
fields.ask: Does this decision unnecessarily close future options or make change expensive?
fields.fix: Prefer decoupled, replaceable, reversible choices where costs are comparable.
fields.good: class Report; def render(formatter); formatter.render(self); end; end

fields.ask: Is visible decay being left in place: dead code, stale references, broken links, or contradictory documentation?
fields.fix: Fix visible decay when encountered instead of normalizing it.

fields.ask: Is disorder accumulating through inconsistent names, exceptions, stale conventions, or abandoned paths?
fields.fix: Remove drift and consolidate exceptions before they become a second system.

fields.source: The Pragmatic Programmer — don't outrun your headlights
fields.ask: Is the design specifying distant hypothetical scenarios more precisely than current evidence allows?
fields.fix: Take small deliberate steps and reassess after each measured result.

fields.ask: Is a hard-to-reverse decision being made when a reversible option provides the same present value?
fields.fix: Prefer rollback paths, replaceable boundaries, and staged changes.

fields.source: A Philosophy of Software Design — Design it Twice
fields.ask: Was a consequential design committed without considering at least one materially different approach?
fields.fix: Sketch and compare alternatives before committing.

fields.ask: Do tests check only a few examples when the important invariant can be stated as a property?
fields.fix: State the invariant and exercise many generated cases.

fields.ask: Where several valid implementations exist, is the chosen one presented as universally correct instead of justified by context?
fields.fix: State the access pattern, failure mode, or constraint that makes the choice fit.
fields.good: # sync: bounded local workload; async would add coordination cost

fields.ask: Does a component hold broader authority than its task requires?
fields.fix: Grant exactly the required scope for exactly the required duration.

fields.ask: Does the default path permit access when no explicit rule granted it?
fields.fix: Default to denial and require an explicit grant.

fields.ask: Is authority checked once and then trusted across later accesses whose state may have changed?
fields.fix: Re-check authority at each access boundary.

fields.ask: Is the security-critical path too large or branchy to inspect and verify as a small mechanism?
fields.fix: Shrink and isolate the trusted path.
fields.bad: def authorize; 1200 lines of mixed parsing, IO and policy; end

fields.ask: Does the secure path impose enough friction that users are pushed toward an unsafe shortcut?
fields.fix: Make the safe path the easy path and remove unnecessary security ceremony.

fields.source: Yaron Minsky — make illegal states unrepresentable
fields.ask: Can an invalid combination of fields or values be constructed at all, or must every caller remember a runtime check?
fields.fix: Encode the invariant in the data shape, constructor, type, or boundary.

fields.ask: Is the same input re-checked at many call sites instead of being parsed once into a value carrying the guarantee?
fields.fix: Parse once at the boundary and pass the proven value inward.
fields.bad: def send(url); raise unless url.start_with?("https:"); fetch(url); end

fields.ask: Can this API be called in the wrong order, with swappable same-typed arguments, or in a meaningless state?
fields.fix: Make invalid sequences or arguments difficult or impossible to express.

fields.source: Richard Cook — How Complex Systems Fail; resilience engineering
fields.ask: Does this path assume the happy case or rely on a single safeguard with no defined degraded mode?
fields.fix: Define independent safeguards and a bounded degraded mode.

fields.ask: Does this artifact have one identifiable center of meaning that its parts reinforce, or is it a flat bag of unrelated pieces?
fields.fix: Strengthen the central purpose and remove or relocate unrelated pieces.
fields.bad: README with unrelated sections on finance, CSS, music, and legal notices
fields.good: README whose sections all explain how to use and govern MASTER

fields.ask: Does the design jump abruptly between granularities without useful intermediate levels?
fields.fix: Introduce meaningful intermediate structure where it clarifies the whole.
fields.bad: system with one 500-line method and 2-line helpers

fields.ask: Does this file perform expensive operations without checking relevant preconditions or bounds?
fields.fix: Check prerequisites, estimate cost, and bound the operation before executing it.

fields.source: The Pragmatic Programmer — avoid artificial coupling
fields.ask: Are unrelated concepts coupled merely because they share a container, proximity, or formatting convention?
fields.fix: Separate unrelated concerns and couple only through meaningful interfaces.
fields.bad: settings = { audio: audio, billing: billing, css: css }

fields.ask: Does this name clearly reveal intent without requiring a comment to decode it?
fields.fix: Rename around the domain action, value, or invariant.

fields.source: Ruby/JS style — trailing commas in multiline literals
fields.ask: Does a multiline collection or argument list omit a trailing comma that stabilizes diffs?
fields.fix: Add the trailing comma to multiline collections and argument lists.

fields.ask: Does a successful operation emit output that the operator does not need?
fields.fix: Report errors and meaningful state; stay quiet on ordinary success.

fields.ask: Are invariant trig, noise, or lookup calculations repeated per frame or per object?
fields.fix: Precompute invariant values once and reuse them.
fields.good: sin_quarter = Math.sin(Math::PI / 4); objects.each { |o| angle = sin_quarter * o.scale }

fields.ask: Do visual elements jump erratically because raw audio samples drive motion directly?
fields.fix: Smooth or envelope audio-derived control values before applying visual motion.

fields.ask: Does this run at full quality until resource exhaustion instead of degrading in measured stages?
fields.fix: Start with a safe baseline and progressively add quality within resource bounds.

fields.ask: Is generated audio unnaturally perfect because noise floor, saturation, timing drift, or humanized variation has been eliminated entirely?
fields.fix: Introduce restrained, purposeful imperfection where the aesthetic calls for it.
fields.good: notes.each { |n| synth.play(n, velocity: humanize(n), at: drift(n.beat)) }

fields.ask: Does this code or document use generic terms where the domain has a clearer established term?
fields.fix: Use the vocabulary the domain actually uses.

fields.ask: Are names vague, generic, or misleading enough that a reader cannot tell what they hold or do?
fields.fix: Choose names that expose role, value, or domain meaning.

fields.ask: Does an error or rejection omit the context needed to locate the cause and decide the next action?
fields.fix: Include relevant operation, subject, and cause without leaking secrets.

fields.ask: Is a comment compensating for code or prose that could instead be rewritten to make the intent obvious?
fields.fix: Refactor the underlying artifact first; keep comments for rationale that cannot be encoded directly.

fields.ask: Does this boundary reject safely normalizable valid variation or emit unnecessarily strict structure that callers do not need?
fields.fix: Normalize harmless variation at the boundary and keep emitted contracts deliberate.

fields.ask: Is a change removing or altering behavior that callers may already depend on despite it never being formally documented?
fields.fix: Search actual consumers and observed behavior before changing the contract; preserve or version what is relied upon.
fields.good: Logger.write("ok") # callers depend on audit output

fields.ask: Must callers invoke methods in a specific order without the API enforcing that sequence?
fields.fix: Encode required state transitions or provide one operation representing the valid sequence.

fields.ask: Is business or decision logic tangled with IO, rendering, or external APIs so isolated tests become difficult?
fields.fix: Move decisions into a testable core and keep the boundary object thin.

fields.ask: Is the code close to a known reusable pattern whose extraction would genuinely reduce complexity rather than add ceremony?
fields.fix: Extract a pattern only when recurring structure earns the abstraction.
fields.bad: if cache.hit?; cache.read; else; fetch; cache.write; end

fields.source: SOLID — Single Responsibility Principle (Robert C. Martin)
fields.ask: Does this class or module have more than one reason to change?
fields.fix: Give each responsibility a distinct owner and boundary.
fields.bad: class Invoice; def calculate; end; def render; end; def email; end; end
fields.good: class Invoice; def calculate; end; end; class InvoiceRenderer; end; class InvoiceMailer; end

fields.ask: Must existing core code be modified whenever a new supported variant is added?
fields.fix: Extend through stable interfaces, registries, or composition where that reduces repeated core edits.
fields.bad: case format; when :json; render_json; when :xml; render_xml; end

fields.ask: Does a subtype violate assumptions or guarantees established by the type it replaces?
fields.fix: Make subtype behavior satisfy the established contract or use a different abstraction.
fields.bad: class ReadOnlyStore < Store; def save(x); raise "no"; end; end

fields.ask: Does an interface force implementations to stub or ignore methods they do not need?
fields.fix: Split broad interfaces into focused contracts.
fields.bad: class Printer; def print; end; def scan; raise NotImplementedError; end; end

fields.ask: Does high-level policy directly instantiate concrete dependencies that should be replaceable?
fields.fix: Depend on stable abstractions and inject concrete implementations at the boundary.
fields.bad: class Checkout; def call; Stripe::Charge.create; end; end
fields.good: class Checkout; def initialize(payments:); @payments = payments; end; end

fields.source: SRP / Unix philosophy — do one thing
fields.ask: Does this module handle unrelated responsibilities instead of one coherent job?
fields.fix: Give the module one job and compose it with neighboring modules.
fields.bad: class UserService; def find; end; def email; end; def export; end; end
fields.good: class UserFinder; end; class UserMailer; end; class UserExporter; end

fields.ask: Is this operation monolithic when it could be cleanly composed from smaller independent parts?
fields.fix: Expose small units with explicit inputs and outputs so they can be composed.

fields.ask: Does this code reach through several objects or expose knowledge of a collaborator's internals?
fields.fix: Talk only to immediate collaborators and encapsulate the traversal.

fields.ask: Is inheritance being used mainly for code reuse rather than a genuine substitutability relationship?
fields.fix: Prefer composition when behavior can vary independently of type identity.
fields.good: class Report; def initialize(formatter:); @formatter = formatter; end; end

fields.source: Clean Code — one level of abstraction per function
fields.ask: Does this function mix policy-level operations with low-level representation or IO details?
fields.fix: Keep each function at one conceptual level and delegate detail downward.
fields.bad: def checkout; authorize_card; db.execute("INSERT INTO..."); render_html; end
fields.good: def checkout; authorize_card; persist_order; render_receipt; end

fields.ask: Does the code fail to read top-down from high-level intent into progressively smaller details?
fields.fix: Arrange definitions so each step introduces the detail used by the next.
fields.bad: def helper; end; def main; helper; end
fields.good: def main; helper; end; def helper; end

fields.ask: Does third-party API or framework surface leak directly into core logic?
fields.fix: Translate external contracts at a boundary and keep the core independent.

fields.ask: Are unexplained numeric literals or booleans carrying domain meaning instead of named concepts?
fields.fix: Name the domain meaning and keep the value in one source.

fields.ask: Does the system defer reporting a known invalid state instead of stopping at the point it is detected?
fields.fix: Reject invalid state immediately with actionable context.

fields.ask: Would repeating the same operation with the same intended input produce an unintended different result?
fields.fix: Make repeat calls converge to the same state or use an idempotency key.
fields.bad: POST /payments creates another charge every retry

fields.ask: Is external or untrusted input used without checking its shape, range, encoding, or allowed values?
fields.fix: Validate or parse input at the boundary before it reaches trusted logic.

fields.ask: Does this function silently modify external state in addition to returning its conceptual result?
fields.fix: Separate side effects from pure transformation where practical.

fields.ask: Does this function depend on hidden mutable state or ambient inputs that callers cannot see?
fields.fix: Pass dependencies explicitly and keep deterministic logic pure.
fields.good: def total(items, tax_rate:); items.sum * tax_rate; end

fields.ask: Are primitives carrying domain rules that would be clearer and safer as a value object?
fields.fix: Create a focused value object when the primitive has behavior or invariants.

fields.ask: Is this method more interested in another object's data than its own?
fields.fix: Move the behavior toward the data it operates on or extract a suitable collaborator.
fields.bad: def total(order); order.items.sum { |i| i.price * i.qty }; end
fields.good: class Order; def total; items.sum { |i| i.price * i.qty }; end; end

fields.ask: Does this class mostly delegate methods to another object without adding meaningful policy?
fields.fix: Remove the unnecessary middle layer or give it a real abstraction.
fields.bad: def name; @user.name; end; def email; @user.email; end

fields.ask: Is this class too small or trivial to justify a separate abstraction boundary?
fields.fix: Inline or merge it unless the boundary provides independent value.
fields.bad: class NameHelper; def call(x); x.name; end; end

fields.ask: Is one class repeatedly changed for several unrelated causes?
fields.fix: Separate the responsibilities so each has a focused reason to change.
fields.bad: class Report; def html; end; def csv; end; def tax; end; def mail; end; end
fields.good: class Report; end; class ReportTax; end; class ReportMailer; end

fields.ask: Is code generalized for a future requirement that has no present evidence or consumer?
fields.fix: Remove speculative hooks and add abstraction when a real use case arrives.

fields.ask: Does one class access another class's internals instead of using its public contract?
fields.fix: Expose the needed behavior through the owner's interface.

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #1 — Visibility of system status
fields.ask: Does a long-running operation provide enough timely feedback for the user to know what is happening?
fields.fix: Show meaningful progress, current state, or the last completed checkpoint.
fields.bad: export_all_records # runs for minutes with no output

fields.source: Visual hierarchy — information scent, typographic scale, Gestalt grouping
fields.ask: On the rendered surface, can a first-time reader distinguish the primary task/content, supporting information, and tertiary controls at a glance? Does visual emphasis follow the user's current goal rather than decoration or implementation convenience?
fields.fix: Name the primary, secondary and tertiary elements for the task; use the existing type, spacing and contrast tokens to establish their order; verify the result in rendered screenshots at mobile and desktop widths without hiding required actions.
fields.bad: A product card gives its seller metadata, badge, price, title and purchase action equal size and contrast.
fields.good: A product title and price lead; seller metadata supports the choice; the purchase action is unmistakable and secondary actions remain quieter.

fields.source: Visibility of system status — contextual, persistent, actionable feedback
fields.ask: At the point a user must decide or wait, does the interface explain the relevant state, what changed, and what action is available next? Is essential meaning retained after transient motion or color feedback ends?
fields.fix: Show truthful status beside the affected task; use persistent text or semantics for success and failure, announce important asynchronous updates accessibly, and provide a concrete recovery action when one exists.
fields.bad: A save button spins briefly, returns to its idle appearance, and leaves the user unsure whether the save succeeded.
fields.good: The save action reports progress, then a persistent saved state; a failure explains the problem and offers a relevant retry path.

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #3 — User control and freedom
fields.ask: Can the user cancel or undo a consequential operation when doing so is technically feasible?
fields.fix: Provide an explicit cancel, undo, or rollback path.
fields.bad: publish! # irreversible and no cancel path

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #9 — help users recover from errors
fields.ask: Does an error explain what happened and what the user can do next?
fields.fix: State the failed operation, relevant cause, and concrete recovery action.
fields.good: raise Error, "invoice 42: payment declined; update card and retry"

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #8 — aesthetic and minimalist design
fields.ask: Does this output contain information that does not earn its place for the current task?
fields.fix: Remove redundant status, decoration, and secondary detail from the primary path.
fields.bad: render title: title, debug: true, metadata: metadata, raw: raw

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #2 — match between system and real world
fields.ask: Does the interface expose implementation jargon where a familiar real-world term would be clearer?
fields.fix: Use the user's domain vocabulary for labels, actions, and concepts.

fields.source: Nielsen Heuristic #6 — recognition rather than recall
fields.ask: Does the user need to remember information across steps that could be shown at the point of use?
fields.fix: Keep relevant context, choices, and state visible where decisions happen.
fields.bad: form.step(4) # requires remembering which file was selected

fields.ask: Does the interface serve only novices or only experts when defaults and accelerators could coexist?
fields.fix: Provide a sensible default plus efficient shortcuts for experienced users.

fields.ask: When the user gets stuck, is concrete, searchable, task-focused help available near the action?
fields.fix: Provide focused guidance where the question arises, with an actionable next step.
fields.bad: button "Deploy" # no explanation or error guidance
fields.good: button "Deploy"; help "Build and release the current revision"

fields.ask: Are the same concepts, actions, or states named or presented differently in different places?
fields.fix: Choose one vocabulary and interaction pattern and reuse it.

fields.ask: Are LLM calls made without exposing enough token or cost information to the operator when that information is available?
fields.fix: Surface measured input, output, and cost data at the appropriate operator boundary.

fields.ask: Is the same expensive LLM request repeated when the input and relevant context are unchanged?
fields.fix: Cache deterministic or safely repeatable requests with an explicit invalidation boundary.

fields.ask: Does a boolean argument make one function perform two different jobs or select unrelated behavior?
fields.fix: Split the responsibilities into named operations or objects.

fields.ask: Does this function mutate an input argument to return a result indirectly?
fields.fix: Return the result explicitly instead of using output parameters.

fields.ask: Is an argument used mainly as a switch between distinct behaviors rather than as data?
fields.fix: Expose distinct operations or strategy objects instead of hiding a dispatch behind a flag.

fields.ask: Are important preconditions, postconditions, and invariants left implicit at an interface?
fields.fix: State and enforce the contract at the boundary.
fields.bad: def divide(a, b); a / b; end
fields.good: def divide(a, b); raise ArgumentError if b.zero?; a / b; end

fields.source: A Philosophy of Software Design — define errors out of existence
fields.ask: Is the interface handling errors that could instead be prevented by making invalid states unrepresentable or normalizing inputs earlier?
fields.fix: Redesign the interface so the problematic state cannot arise on the normal path.

fields.source: API design — minimize public surface area
fields.ask: Is the public interface larger than necessary, exposing entry points or exceptions callers do not need?
fields.fix: Reduce the public contract to the smallest useful surface and keep internals private.
fields.bad: class Client; def fetch; end; def retry; end; def parse; end; def raw_response; end; end
fields.good: class Client; def fetch; end; end

fields.ask: Does this present all complexity at once instead of revealing detail as the user's task requires it?
fields.fix: Lead with the common path and reveal advanced controls when they become relevant.

fields.ask: Does this perform substantial work without reporting progress, checkpoints, or a recoverable state?
fields.fix: Add meaningful progress or checkpoints proportional to operation duration and risk.

fields.ask: Does this class mainly hold data while behavior that belongs with that data is scattered across other modules?
fields.fix: Move cohesive behavior toward the data owner or replace the holder with a meaningful domain abstraction.
fields.good: class Money; attr_reader :cents; def taxed(rate); cents * rate; end; end

fields.ask: Does adding a type in one hierarchy require adding a corresponding type in another hierarchy?
fields.fix: Collapse the parallel hierarchies or compose the varying dimensions.

fields.ask: Does a subtype or variant inherit capabilities it cannot honor and then reject or ignore most of them?
fields.fix: Choose an abstraction that matches the subtype's real contract or use composition.
fields.bad: class ReadOnly < Writable; def write; raise NotImplementedError; end; end

fields.source: Strunk, Elements of Style — put statements in positive form
fields.ask: Is a statement phrased as a negation when a direct positive verb or construction says the same thing more clearly?
fields.fix: Prefer the direct positive form when it preserves meaning.
fields.bad: He did not remember the password.

fields.source: Strunk, Elements of Style — coordinate ideas in similar form
fields.ask: Do items in a list or series mix grammatical forms where parallel structure would make the relationship clearer?
fields.fix: Use the same grammatical form for coordinated items.
fields.bad: The system must read files, validation, and to report errors.
fields.good: The system must read files, validate input, and report errors.

fields.source: Strunk, Elements of Style — keep related words together
fields.ask: Is a modifier or subject separated from its referent so the sentence misreads on the first pass?
fields.fix: Keep words that belong together close enough that the intended relation is immediate.
fields.bad: The operator, after checking the logs carefully, restarted the service.
fields.good: After checking the logs carefully, the operator restarted the service.

fields.source: Strunk, Elements of Style — paragraph as the unit
fields.ask: Does a paragraph mix unrelated topics or bury its main point below secondary detail?
fields.fix: Give each paragraph one controlling topic and state its point early.
fields.bad: The paragraph opens with deployment history, then discusses pricing, then explains the test failure.
fields.good: The paragraph opens with the test failure and explains its cause and fix.

fields.source: Grice — cooperative principle (quantity, quality, relation, manner)
fields.ask: Does this communication say too much or too little, assert what is unverified, drift off-topic, or obscure the point through needless complexity?
fields.fix: Provide the needed information, qualify uncertain claims, stay relevant, and make the path clear.
fields.bad: The system is definitely perfect and, by the way, here are unrelated implementation details.
fields.good: The test passed locally; CI has not run yet.

fields.ask: Does every detector or check that can influence a decision have a known-positive and known-negative proof, or an explicit semantic evaluation path?
fields.practice: A measuring instrument must demonstrate what it catches and what it spares before its findings can drive automatic action.
fields.fix: Add polarity fixtures or a semantic evaluation contract before trusting the instrument.
fields.bad: A new veto regex is enabled with no false-positive fixture.
fields.good: The detector has a failing fixture, a clean fixture, and its evaluation surface is covered by a check.

fields.ask: Does this claim of completion have direct evidence from the actual resulting artifact or executed check, rather than intention, absence of an error, or an unrun test?
fields.practice: Completion is an observed state, not a promise.
fields.fix: Run the relevant proof and report the observed result; otherwise report the work as unresolved.
fields.bad: Done because the patch was written.
fields.good: Done after the changed code, relevant tests and final state were actually inspected.

fields.ask: Did an unavailable dependency, skipped probe, timeout, missing permission, or unmeasured check get treated as success?
fields.practice: Unknown, skipped and unavailable are distinct from pass.
fields.fix: Return an explicit inconclusive/degraded result and preserve the unresolved evidence.
fields.bad: Browser unavailable, therefore visual check passed.
fields.good: Browser unavailable, visual check inconclusive, no completion claim.

fields.ask: Does a ratchet or threshold change preserve its meaning, or was the threshold moved merely to absorb new debt or make the current tree pass?
fields.practice: A ratchet may make progress harder to lose, never easier to redefine.
fields.fix: Keep the existing threshold or justify a measured structural improvement before changing it.
fields.bad: Increase the allowed violation count because the scan found more violations.
fields.good: Remove violations first, then tighten or preserve the threshold against the improved baseline.

fields.ask: Is this finding sufficiently deterministic that an automatic edit can be applied without guessing at user intent or hidden semantics?
fields.practice: LLM-generated text is not evidence that an automatic transformation is safe.
fields.fix: Downgrade to review-only or add deterministic evidence and preservation tests before automatic repair.
fields.bad: A semantic smell triggers an automatic rewrite because the model produced plausible code.
fields.good: Only a deterministic, fixture-proven transformation is eligible for automatic repair.

fields.source: laws.yml SINGULARITY — one source of truth; the DRY principle of The Pragmatic Programmer
fields.ask: Does this change define a fact, rule, threshold or type a second time when an existing definition already owns it, so the two copies can drift apart?
fields.practice: Every fact has one owner; everything else reads it.
fields.fix: Find the existing owner and read from it. If none exists, create one and move every copy onto it in the same change.
fields.bad: Add a second Law type whose members mirror the one in the kernel, each carrying its own copy of the same threshold.
fields.good: Reuse the kernel's Law type and read the threshold from the single file that owns it.

fields.source: laws.yml LINEARITY — sequential flow with minimal branches; cyclomatic complexity, McCabe 1976
fields.ask: Does this change make the path through the code harder to follow in order, with deeper nesting, extra branches, or control flow that jumps back and forth instead of running top to bottom?
fields.practice: Read the code once, top to bottom, and arrive at the result.
fields.fix: Flatten with guard clauses, extract the branch that breaks the sequence, and order steps as they run.
fields.bad: Nest three conditionals inside a loop so the success path sits at the deepest indent.
fields.good: Return early on each failure, then run the success path unindented to the end.

fields.source: laws.yml ROBUSTNESS — safe failure, security and edge-case handling
fields.ask: Across this artifact and its real operating context, what can fail unsafely under invalid input, adversarial use, concurrency, resource pressure, missing dependencies, or partial failure? Name only evidenced failure paths; return CLEAN when the relevant boundary fails safely.
fields.practice: Treat every boundary and degraded state as a first-class path, not as an exception to the design.
fields.fix: Close the concrete unsafe path, preserve useful failure context, and prove both the bad and safe paths.
fields.bad: The happy path succeeds, so malformed input and provider failure are assumed safe.
fields.good: Input, authorization, resource bounds and failure recovery have explicit evidence-backed behavior.

fields.source: laws.yml PROXIMITY — related concepts stay close and cohesive
fields.ask: Are related responsibilities, evidence, states, controls or visual elements separated so far that their relationship is hard to understand or keep consistent? Evaluate semantic, structural and visual proximity for this artifact; return CLEAN when the grouping communicates the real relationships.
fields.practice: Keep pieces together when they change together; separate them when they have distinct ownership.
fields.fix: Move or group the related elements at the boundary that best reflects their shared responsibility without adding another abstraction layer.
fields.bad: A control is separated from its state, or related logic is duplicated across unrelated modules.
fields.good: The structure groups each responsibility and the interface groups information by its actual relationship.

fields.source: laws.yml ABSTRACTION — appropriate boundaries and information hiding
fields.ask: Does this artifact expose implementation detail, hide a load-bearing contract, or introduce an abstraction whose indirection exceeds the problem it solves? Assess the boundary in code, prose, behavior and presentation; return CLEAN when the boundary makes the concept easier to use and verify.
fields.practice: Hide volatile mechanics behind a small truthful contract; do not hide important behavior behind ceremony.
fields.fix: Expose the needed contract, encapsulate the unstable detail, or delete the abstraction if direct expression is clearer.
fields.bad: Callers depend on undocumented internals or traverse an abstraction that adds no useful policy.
fields.good: The public surface is small, intent-revealing and sufficient to exercise the behavior.

fields.source: laws.yml DENSITY — signal over noise and no needless information
fields.ask: Does any part of this artifact consume attention without adding relevant meaning, evidence, action or necessary context? Look across code, prose, UI, status output and visual ornament; return CLEAN when every element earns its place.
fields.practice: Prefer the shortest complete expression, not the shortest expression that omits a necessary fact.
fields.fix: Remove repetition and ornament, then restore any evidence or context needed to make the result complete.
fields.bad: Repeated labels, redundant prose, decoration or duplicated logic competes with the actual task.
fields.good: Each statement, control, visual emphasis and abstraction contributes distinct useful meaning.

fields.source: laws.yml RENDERED_VALUES — rendered values and presentation are operator-owned
fields.ask: Are colors, typography, sounds, motion, spacing, layout, content, or rendered behavior invented independently of their canonical owner or altered without evidence and approval? For nonvisual artifacts, assess other operator-owned values and contracts; return CLEAN when values remain sourced, truthful and intentional.
fields.practice: Read canonical values and preserve real-world fidelity; never invent a competing design or configuration authority.
fields.fix: Use the owning token, configuration, source asset or explicit operator decision and verify the actual rendered result.
fields.bad: A second color/font/spacing table drifts from the canonical tokens, or a visual claim is made without inspecting the render.
fields.good: Values flow from their owning source, original media stays truthful, and rendered evidence confirms the outcome.
